name: Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy
definition: Clinical spinal cord dysfunction caused by degenerative cervical cord compression; diagnosis requires symptoms/signs correlated with imaging.

typical: Hand clumsiness or loss of dexterity
Upper motor-neuron signs may be present

redFlags.item: Severe gait decline or major weakness

differentials: Multiple sclerosis or other cord disease

investigations.principle: Neurological examination and cervical MRI are central when myelopathy is suspected.
investigations.MRI: Assess cord compression, levels, canal narrowing and intramedullary signal change; correlate with clinical severity.

green: Avoid unnecessary delay in specialist evaluation when clinical myelopathy is present
amber: This is not a routine neck-pain pathway; progressive myelopathy generally requires prompt spine-specialist assessment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: No direct Ayurvedic equivalence is assigned. Any Vata-related neurological correlation remains scholarly and unvalidated.

patientEducation.summary: Clinical spinal cord dysfunction caused by degenerative cervical cord compression; diagnosis requires symptoms/signs correlated with imaging.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.

sources.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Cervical Pain or Cervical Radiculopathy — Revised 2024
